summary: The three assertions round 3 asked for are all genuinely pinned, verified by re-applying each named mutation to the staged bytes rather than by reading the fix: (1) appending grant.url() to the Push guard message reds aMISMATCHEDViaAndGrantIsRefused; (2) EMPTY -> new byte[]{9} in deliver's Push construction reds theGrantNamesTheSegmentBeingSERVED and nothing else; (3) replacing publish's per-segment collect with a rethrow reds aSIGNINGFailureNamesTheSegmentAndDoesNotRollBack (and the sibling store-failure case). None is a fix written from the same sentence as the finding. Eight further mutations measured: the r1 coalescing mutation, the r2 neighbouring-key and fan-out-literal mutations, the TTL ceiling widening and the AssemblingSubscriber grant drop are all killed by exactly the case that claims them. Baseline :ingest:test 252 tests / 0 failures before and after; tree restored and re-verified green. ONE NEW MAJOR: the ROOT-logger probe in theGrantReachesNOLogLine is a weaker re-implementation of GrantNeverLoggedTest.capturing, which lives in the same package -- it drops record.getParameters() and drops the System.out/System.err swap, and TWO measured leaks of the signed URL on the new serving path leave the whole module green. Criterion 3 is therefore pinned only for the concatenated-message form.

findings.title: the new ROOT-logger probe is weaker than the one already in the same package: it drops record.getParameters() and the stream swap, and two leaks of the signed URL on the new serving path survive
findings.failure_scenario: TWO MEASURED MUTATIONS, EACH ALONE, EACH LEAVING THE WHOLE :ingest:test GREEN (252 tests, 0 failures; DirectServingTest 13/13). Applied in SubscriptionHub.deliver immediately after the hoisted mint, i.e. on the exact line this row adds. (a) PARAMETER FORM: `System.getLogger("binjava.ingest.SubscriptionHub").log(System.Logger.Level.INFO, "serving {0} direct via {1}", segmentKey, grant.url());` -- green. CONTROL, to prove the gap is precisely getParameters() and not a dead probe: the identical leak written with concatenation, `LOG.log(INFO, "serving " + segmentKey + " direct via " + grant.url())`, DOES turn theGrantReachesNOLogLine red. The probe at DirectServingTest.java:492-498 appends only record.getLevel(), record.getMessage() and String.valueOf(record.getThrown()); System.Logger's JUL backend puts a format's arguments in LogRecord.setParameters, so the secret never reaches the StringBuilder the assertion at line 526 reads. Passing the Grant record itself as a parameter is the same hole (Grant.toString redacts, but grant.url() as a parameter does not). (b) STREAM FORM: `System.out.println("debug: direct grant " + grant.url());` on the same line -- green. The new probe attaches a JUL handler and nothing else, so a println is invisible to it. WHY THIS IS MAJOR AND NOT A STYLE POINT: the correct instrument already exists 200 lines away in the SAME package -- GrantNeverLoggedTest.capturing (ingest/src/test/java/binjava/ingest/GrantNeverLoggedTest.java:131-173) swaps System.out and System.err, attaches the ROOT handler at Level.ALL, AND walks record.getParameters(), with a javadoc naming 'a debug print left behind' as the case it exists for. The new case re-implements that instrument and drops two of its three channels, so acceptance criterion 3 ('the grant reaches NO log, trace or error message, captured from a handler on the ROOT logger') is pinned only for the concatenated-message form on a path where the grant is in scope on every publish. Unlike r3-t1, no second defect is needed: one added statement in one of the two forms above leaks the signature in production with the suite green. THE KILL IS TO REUSE THE EXISTING INSTRUMENT -- call GrantNeverLoggedTest's capturing (or lift it to a shared helper) instead of hand-rolling a handler, which also removes the second copy of a probe whose lessons cost M5.13 a measurement.

findings.title: the presign javadoc is orphaned by the two new fields and its last paragraph is now false: it tells a reader the clamp is unconstrained
findings.failure_scenario: NO SURVIVING MUTATION IS CLAIMED; the defect is prose that contradicts a measurement. The diff inserts `failSigningWith` and `signings`, each with its own doc comment, BETWEEN the long presign javadoc (StoreFakes.java:258-278) and the presign method it documents -- so javadoc now binds the one-line comment to the field and the long block becomes a dangling comment on nothing. Its closing paragraph still reads 'NOTHING CALLS THIS YET, so the ttl it honours is unconstrained too -- replacing this body with a throw leaves the suite green. M5.45d is the first caller and the row that closes both.' M5.45d IS this commit: presign is called on every direct publish, replacing its body with a throw now reds aSIGNINGFailureNamesTheSegmentAndDoesNotRollBack, and the ttl is pinned -- MEASURED, widening both ceilings to 3600 s reds theTTLIsCLAMPEDToSixtySecondsMeasuredFromTheEPOCH. The failure this invites: a later author extending this fake reads 'unconstrained' and 'leaves the suite green', concludes nothing depends on the EPOCH-relative expiry, and changes it -- which is exactly the trap the same javadoc's first two paragraphs were written to prevent. Move the block back above presign and cut or rewrite the stale paragraph. Raised as a minor and, per review.md rule 11, fixing it is optional.
